A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Flood complex research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support comparison; v2 additionally includes a changelog explaining the experimental revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original approximation, runtime, scalability, classification, and regression results in Section 5, plus GPU and landmark-selection experiments in Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical investigations and reports revised classification and regression results in Tables 2–3 following reruns on the released datasets.

M1.justification: The Flood complex construction, simplex discretization, masking, GPU computation, and downstream prediction pipeline are retained. Wording clarifications do not introduce a new method component or procedure.

E1.justification: The mechanical-components task is substantially revised: v1 combines MCB-A and MCB-B into 2,441 meshes across 21 classes; v2 uses MCB-A alone, yielding 1,745 meshes across 11 classes under the name mcb-c (Appendix A.4). This changes the represented population and label space, rather than merely renaming the benchmark. Other dataset and task coverage is retained.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same comparators, including subsampled, averaged, and full Alpha PH, PointNet++, PointMLP, and PVT. The GPU and landmark-selection comparisons also retain their participants.

E3.justification: ModelNet10 inputs change from 1M to 250k sampled points per mesh and gain coordinate normalization to [-1, 1]. Appendix D also reports new training/validation/test splits and reruns on the released datasets. These materially revise evaluation inputs and partitions, although the ten-split 80/20 design, metrics, and nominal training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The runtime breakdown, scaling studies, subsample-size analysis, GPU comparison, and FPS-versus-random landmark analysis are retained. Appendix B adds no new ablation, robustness test, or supplementary analytical question.

E5.justification: Appendix D newly reports using different point-sampling seeds, and Section 5.3 clarifies averaging metrics over splits. Ten classification splits, mean-plus-standard-deviation reporting, and the 25-run landmark experiment remain; no increased replication or new significance procedure is reported.

E6.justification: Tables 2–3 replace many accuracies, errors, and runtimes. Flood PH accuracy changes from 0.99 to 0.98 on swisscheese, 0.91 to 0.88 on rocks, and 0.79 to 0.77 on corals. The revised MCB task reports 0.74 instead of 0.68, while ModelNet10 reports 0.72 instead of 0.60 and reverses Flood PH's ranking relative to the subsampled Alpha baselines. These are revised-condition results, not demonstrated same-setting gains.

T1.justification: The stability and approximation guarantees, two-dimensional homotopy-equivalence result, Appendix C proofs, and circle example are retained. Parenthesis, notation-placement, and wording corrections do not change the mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and discussion retain the core contributions: the Flood construction, theoretical guarantees, large-scale computation, and usefulness for geometrically complex point clouds. Dataset availability is newly advertised without redefining these scientific claims.

C2.justification: Appendix D newly explains the conflicting-label duplicates introduced by combining MCB-A and MCB-B, and links changed PH accuracies to revised data and more effective time-limited LGBM training on different hardware. Existing explanations involving geometric complexity and diagram vectorization, and the theoretical applicability limitations, remain.

D1.justification: Appendix A.2 newly reports distributing all five prepared classification datasets with predefined splits through flooder and supplies a loading example. Section 5.3 specifies Alpha baseline subsample sizes, while Appendix A.3 revises the hardware disclosure from Ubuntu/EPYC 7313/H100 NVL to SUSE/EPYC 9554/H100 80GB. These substantially expand reproducibility resources and document the changed computing environment.

R1.justification: The literature coverage and substantive positioning remain unchanged. Edelsbrunner and Harer's textbook moves from an existing Appendix C footnote into the bibliography; the added citation beside the averaged Alpha baseline refers to Chazal et al., already discussed for subsampling in v1.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized wording and typographical corrections, adopts mcb-c terminology, revises the experimental narrative, expands the dataset-access explanation, and adds Appendix D's changelog. The main organization and most exposition remain intact.

P2.justification: The same twelve figures and four tables remain. Figure 9 receives modest panel and legend-layout adjustments, Tables 2–3 have limited heading, spacing, and emphasis changes, and Appendix A.2 gains a dataset-loading code block.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses an important empirical defect: the merged MCB benchmark contained duplicate geometries with conflicting labels, and the revised benchmark removes that source of ambiguity. Providing prepared datasets, predefined splits, loading instructions, and explicitly documented reruns also substantially strengthens reproducibility. These gains outweigh the narrower MCB task and reduced ModelNet10 point density; the improvement rests on more reliable evidence and reproducibility, rather than higher scores under changed conditions.
